annotation.title_clean: Legal challenges for robots and autonomous artificial intelligence systems in the healthcare context with special reference to Covid-19 health crisis
annotation.title_en: Legal challenges for robots and autonomous artificial intelligence systems in the healthcare context with special reference to Covid-19 health crisis
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Journal article exploring legal issues raised by healthcare robots and autonomous AI, especially liability for damage and personal data processing, with reference to COVID-19 robots. It argues that reforms of legal doctrine and regulatory structures are needed, drawing on the 2017 European Parliament civil law rules on robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Liability for damage caused by robots and personal data processing are key legal issues in healthcare robotics.
Reforms of legal doctrine and regulatory structures are needed for healthcare robots and AI.
Care robots address ageing and disability needs but require limits on delegating tasks and decisions to machines.
COVID-19 robots such as OPENTRONS for PCR testing show benefits of healthcare robotics.
Relies on the 2017 European Parliament Resolution on civil law rules on robotics as a regulatory reference.
